h2: Maritime NDT around New Orleans: inland barges, towboats and the lower Mississippi
html:
Maritime NDT around New Orleans: inland barges, towboats and the lower Mississippi

Most maritime NDT around New Orleans is brown-water work. It covers inland tank barges, pressure barges and towboats on the Mississippi River System and the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway, plus the docks and terminals along the lower river. The core tasks are thickness gauging, weld crack detection and visual survey for Coast Guard, third-party or class surveyors. Atlantis, based in Houston, sends crews to the yard, fleet or dock.

The river as a working port. The Port of South Louisiana covers a 54-mile stretch of the Mississippi between New Orleans and Baton Rouge. It handled about 248 million short tons in 2023. Grain, soybeans and corn are major exports, and crude oil, petroleum products and chemicals make up much of the rest. The barges that serve this traffic spend time in a shipyard on a regular cycle. There, bottom and side plating is gauged, internal structure is checked for wastage, and renewed steel is examined before the hull goes back into the tow.

Pressure barges and petrochemical cargo. Part of the inland fleet carries pressurized cargoes such as liquefied petroleum gas and ethylene plant co-products, which follow petrochemical growth along the Gulf Coast. Kirby's purchase of Targa's 16 pressure barges, about 258,000 barrels of capacity, shows how specialized that segment is. The cargo tanks on these barges are welded pressure containers. Weld examination and wall-thickness history therefore matter more on them than on an open hopper barge carrying grain.

Subchapter M from the surveyor's side. Third-party organizations are approved by the Coast Guard under 46 CFR Part 139. They audit an operator's Towing Safety Management System against Part 138 and survey individual towboats under Part 137. The Coast Guard has accepted the Responsible Carrier Program of the American Waterways Operators as a TSMS option, and class societies such as ABS also act as third-party organizations. For an NDT crew, the practical point is simple: hull gauging and crack findings feed the surveyor's report. The gauging plan, report format and personnel requirements should be agreed with the surveyor before the boat is out of the water. Atlantis confirms at quotation whether its personnel are acceptable for the survey in question.

Seasons and access. Spring high water on the Mississippi and the June to November hurricane season both change yard and fleeting schedules. Work is planned with float in the dates, and rope access or staging is arranged for dock structures that cannot be reached from the bank.

  • Tank barges: bottom, side and internal structure gauging during yard periods
  • Pressure barges: cargo tank weld examination and thickness history
  • Towboats: hull condition evidence for Part 137 surveys and TSMS audits
  • River docks and terminals: dock piping, mooring structures and loading equipment
  • Reports in the format the third-party organization or class surveyor requires

Where to go next. Searches for maritime NDT services in general are answered on maritime NDT services. How a single written practice can satisfy both the Coast Guard and class survey cycles is covered on maritime NDT consulting in New Orleans. Statewide inspection scopes are on inspection services in Louisiana. For crews you want to train in-house, see maritime NDT training and NDT training in New Orleans. Gauging results can go out as signed reports from the ERP reports app. To scope a yard period, send the barge or towboat details and the survey basis through the New Orleans marine NDT enquiry.
